case_types.name: Cheque bounce
case_types.blurb: Dishonour of a cheque for insufficiency of funds - a criminal complaint. Around 15% of a typical court's caseload; high volume, relatively standard.

practice_notes.quote: For a cheque bounce we always file in the branch's town, not where the drawer lives. The magistrate here knows the bankers, it moves faster.
practice_notes.establishes: Forum choice by local convenience - a habit that sits on top of the §142 jurisdiction rules, not in them.

practice_notes.quote: The registry won't take the complaint without the original memo of dishonour stapled on top, even though the section only needs the fact of return.
practice_notes.establishes: A documentary norm enforced at the counter that is stricter than the statute's own requirement.

practice_notes.quote: Nine out of ten of these settle the day the accused is first summoned. Nobody wants the conviction; they want the money and the compounding.
practice_notes.establishes: The real disposal path - compounding under §147 - dwarfs contested trial, though the Act treats trial as the default.

practice_notes.quote: Banks here file in bulk - a clerk brings fifty complaints in one folder. We've built our own numbering just to keep the batch together.
practice_notes.establishes: Institutional-filer reality that shapes court workflow well before any rule of procedure applies.

rollout_states.name: Kerala
rollout_states.note: Mostly individuals and small companies filing. The original clean-sheet pilot - ~2,000 cases/yr in Kollam. Court language: Malayalam.

rollout_states.name: Gujarat
rollout_states.note: High share of institutional filers - banks and NBFCs - sometimes a thousand cases in a day. Needs bulk filing and case management at scale. Court language: Gujarati.

rollout_states.name: Punjab
rollout_states.note: Requirements captured; own sequencing of the same shared-core process.

rollout_states.name: Sikkim
rollout_states.note: Early engagement - a small jurisdiction with its own local practice.
